newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Lev ends stable as Bulgaria, IMF reach accord.
newsitem.headline: Lev ends stable as Bulgaria, IMF reach accord.

text.p: The lev closed at 1,580-1,590 per dollar, in a tighter spread from the morning's 1,570-1,600 and flat on the previous close amid expectations of a stable lev following a financial accord with the IMF, dealers said.

"There was a rise in dollar supply mainly from final clients today in anticipation of lev stability after the government and the International Monetary Fund said they have reached a funding agreement," one dealer said.

Foreign currency demand was also larger and the central bank was seen as the main dollar buyer today, aiming to boost its foreign exchange reserves ahead of planned introduction of a fixed exchange rate mechanism, the currency board.
Central bank officials declined further comment.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) and Bulgaria's interim cabinet on Monday announced an accord on financial reform and funding worth more than $650 million to stabilise the shattered economy over the next year.
IMF mission leader Anne McGuirk told a news conference a currency board system would be introduced in June to restore confidence in the lev.

Central bank foreign exchange reserves rose by $30.5 million in February to $445.5 million due to central bank net dollar purchases on the interbank market. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
